collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE II: THE LAND, MEMORY AND NEW TRADITIONS (LCB-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
Isola's ceremonies for the land and sea, its ways of remembering and mourning, and the new traditions its people make, question and change: rain songs, reef promises, memory gardens, funerals, forgotten melodies and festivals nobody planned.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: An elder wants a garden where families plant a flower for each person they have lost: start it, or keep the graves as they are.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has an idea: a memory garden behind the graves, where every family can plant a flower for each person they have lost, and come to sit among them. (friend) points out that the space behind the graves is where the children play, and that the village would need to find them somewhere else. What should the village do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The memory garden is planted over a single season. Families come and go, planting, weeding, sitting. The children are moved to a new playing field, and complain for exactly one day. Before long they are bringing flowers to the garden too.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: The village decides to leave the space for the children. (subject) is disappointed, and plants a single flower beside the graves anyway, for (subject.his/her) own lost ones. Within a month there are twenty flowers beside it. The garden is starting itself.
